facts.text: The CLI is organised around three verbs of work: dump ingests, correlate proposes refs, and retrieve (search and compile) reads.
An option a command does not take is rejected on stderr with exit 1, with a suggestion when a known flag is close, and a rejected command writes nothing.
at: An option the command does not take is rejected on stderr with exit 1

facts.text: CLI commands exit 0 on success and 1 on any error; verify --require-current also exits 1 when a cited fact is not live.
at: with `--require-current` it exits 1 when any id is not live

facts.text: init creates the store by constructing a DossierStore, which creates the schema on first use.
dump ingests one file deterministically into facts for one subject: the input is stored as a content-addressed blob and split by markdown heading or kept whole.
Running dump twice on the same file is idempotent: the second run creates nothing and reports every chunk as deduped.
dump only preserves raw bytes by heading or whole file; it does not extract claims or symbols, so the skill says to dump to a separate raw subject.
at: it does not extract claims or symbols

facts.text: post writes a batch of structured facts with declared refs for one subject from a JSON request file, or from stdin when the file is a hyphen.
at: Structured facts with declared refs go in through `dossier post --file <request.json>`

facts.text: post --dry-run runs the full resolution path, reports the same verdicts a real post would give, and writes nothing.
at: same verdicts as a real post, nothing written

facts.text: An invalid item in a batch is rejected with a named error on stderr and the rest of the batch still commits.
at: An invalid item is rejected with a named error and the rest of the batch commits.

facts.text: correlate proposes refs between facts using two deterministic matchers, same_ref and shared_tag.
at: **correlate** proposes refs between facts using deterministic matchers

facts.text: Correlate proposals carry basis derived, are returned and never written, and are never asserted as truth.
at: Proposals carry basis `derived`, are returned and never written

facts.text: The same_ref matcher ignores the locator, so facts sharing one file ref pair all-to-all and a store-wide run hits the 200-proposal cap at about 15 such facts.
at: a store-wide run hits the 200-proposal cap

facts.text: check resolves a subject, summarises what is already known (fact and conflict counts plus the top claims), and can judge draft facts without writing.
check's summary lists at most 8 top facts with text capped at 120 characters.
at: top: at most 8, text capped at 120 chars

facts.text: search finds facts by text and filters, including reverse-impact lookup of the facts that carry a ref to a given target.
A plain query term that FTS5 would misread as syntax, such as Self-taught or us-east-1, is quoted and searched as a phrase, while real FTS5 syntax still works.
search returns 20 hits by default and at most 100, with total, complete and a next cursor for keyset paging.
search --brief returns one short line per hit: id, kind, status and the first 120 characters of text.
at: id, kind, status, first 120 chars of text

facts.text: show prints one fact with its refs, attachments and the inbound facts that reference it.
at: Print one fact with its refs, attachments and inbound referrers.

facts.text: verify takes fact ids and reports the derived status of each, read in one snapshot: live, superseded, retracted, stale, contested or unknown, with the reason.
at: `verify` takes fact ids and reports the derived status of each

facts.text: verify accepts at most 200 ids, answers a repeated id once and writes nothing.
verify --require-current exits 1 unless every id is live, so it can gate a script; the answer is still printed.
changes prints the journal page that /api/changes serves: rows after a cursor, or the newest rows, optionally for one subject.
A changes page holds 100 rows by default and at most 500, and a last or limit below 1 is rejected.
retract tombstones one fact by id.
at: | `dossier retract` | Retract a fact by id. |

facts.text: There is no retract tool over MCP: retraction is a CLI verb only.
at: There is no retract tool: retraction is a CLI verb.

facts.text: dossier compile compiles the cited, budgeted dossier for one subject, as JSON or markdown.
With --descendants a compile covers the subject's subtree, stopping 3 levels below it.
Every emitted fact in a markdown dossier ends with its fact id in brackets, so every line is cited.
at: every emitted fact id appears in brackets

facts.text: publish exports the store as a self-describing bundle an agent can read from a repository with no MCP server, daemon or network.
at: exports the store as a self-describing bundle of markdown files

facts.text: publish writes a markdown bundle by default, or a line-oriented JSONL data bundle with --format jsonl.
at: `--format md` (the default) writes the markdown bundle

facts.text: A bundle holds live facts only: superseded and retracted facts and facts of kind dossier are not published.
at: superseded, retracted and kind `dossier` facts are not

facts.text: Identical inputs produce byte-identical bundle files and unchanged files are not rewritten.
A published fact file is named from the fact's content, not its random store id, so re-importing the same facts gives the same file names.
A profile is a small JSON file of a consumer's limits; publish checks the bundle against it and with --respect-limits repacks it into shards.
at: A **profile** is a small JSON file of limits

facts.text: import rebuilds a store from a markdown or JSONL bundle and picks the reader itself.
at: accepts a markdown bundle or a JSONL bundle

facts.text: import only works into an empty database: a subject or fact that already exists fails the import.
at: already exists in the store; import into an empty database

facts.text: The JSONL reader treats a bundle as untrusted: it reads only files the manifest lists and verifies each data file's bytes, lines and sha256 before committing anything.
at: The JSONL reader treats the bundle as untrusted

facts.text: Round tripping needs a bundle published with fact files; only what a bundle holds is restored, so superseded and retracted facts are not imported.
mcp serves newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio; only protocol messages are written to stdout.
at: **MCP.** `dossier mcp` serves newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio

facts.text: serve starts the loopback web UI, on port 8787 unless --port says otherwise.
version, also spelled --version, prints the product version and nothing else.
Each MCP tool is a thin call into the same DossierStore method the CLI calls, through the transport-neutral Ops class.
The server only answers calls: it implements no subscriptions, sampling or elicitation, so it cannot push a request to an agent.
A failed tool call returns isError true with an envelope holding a stable machine-readable code and a message.
The MCP tool dump is the CLI verb dump.
The MCP tool post_facts is the CLI verb post, and stamps each fact with the calling client's identity.
The MCP tool correlate is the CLI verb correlate.
The MCP tool search is the CLI verb search, with brief as an argument.
The MCP tool check is the CLI verb check, taking drafts as an array.
The MCP tool get_fact is the CLI verb show.
The MCP tool verify_facts is the CLI verb verify.
The MCP tool changes is the CLI verb changes.
The MCP tool compile_dossier is the CLI verb dossier compile.
The web server listens on loopback only and refuses a request for any other Host with a 4xx, so a page reached through a rebound DNS name cannot read the store.
at: a request for any other `Host` is refused with a 4xx

facts.text: The JSON endpoints are /api/subjects, /api/search, /api/compile, /api/fact, /api/graph, /api/revision and /api/changes, plus the /api/events stream.
The web surface is read-only: a POST to any endpoint is answered 405.
The page's scripts are served as files under a Content-Security-Policy that allows no inline script.
The loopback web UI has no login.
at: the loopback web UI has no login

facts.text: /api/events is a Server-Sent Events stream: a baseline revision, then the journal as changes frames, and a reset when the resume point fell out of retention.
The stream polls the revision every 500 ms and sends changes frames of at most 200 rows, draining up to 5,000 rows per tick.
at: a page of at most 200 rows, up to 5,000 rows drained per tick

facts.text: A reconnecting client resumes from Last-Event-ID, which wins over ?since=N.
Eight event streams run concurrently and the ninth gets 503 busy.
While idle the stream writes a keepalive comment every five seconds.
The graph view draws a bounded neighbourhood of a subject on a canvas and can expand a node in place.
/api/graph takes depth 0 to 3 (default 1) and max_nodes 1 to 2000 (default 500), and nodes never exceed max_nodes.
A graph edge is emitted only when both ends are in the payload; hidden ends are reported in unresolved and counted in truncated, not drawn.
at: Edges: an edge is emitted only when both ends are in the payload.

facts.text: Symbol and other external refs stay on their fact in the graph and are never nodes.
at: Symbol and other external refs stay on their fact

facts.text: The graph view is live: it listens on /api/events and re-fetches just the subject a change row names, falling back to polling /api/changes every second.
The activity feed under the graph bar shows one line per journal row and keeps the newest 80, every value rendered as text.
The graph view shows a fact's stored status, so a stale or contested fact reads live there.
at: the change journal and the graph view carry the stored status
